name: Foliot Furniture
old_description: We invest in safe, well-run facilities, fair pay, and ongoing skills development across our 630+ person workforce. Since 2019, we have reduced recordable workplace injuries by nearly 80%. Our team benefits from on-site training, wellness programs, a bistro, a gym, collective insurance, and continuous professional development opportunities.
about:
Foliot Furniture was founded in 1991 in Montreal, Quebec, by Daniel Foliot, a former aspiring lawyer who sold his stake in a woodworking company to start his own venture. The company is now headquartered in Las Vegas, Nevada, and operates three manufacturing facilities across the United States and Canada. A 2020 investment from private equity firm Novacap supports its continued expansion.

The company designs, engineers, and manufactures commercial furniture in-house for high-use environments including student housing, hospitality, community living, government, staff housing, and maritime sectors. Its vertically integrated operation spans a 309,000-square-foot factory in Las Vegas, a 40,000-square-foot facility in Canada, and a newer Canadian plant producing laminate panels. With a workforce of over 630 people, Foliot has delivered furniture for more than 1.25 million rooms across North America.

Clients include universities such as Savannah College of Art and Design and Cornell University, hospitality brands like Hilton and LivSmart Studios, and organizations including WestCare, UNLV/Mojave Counseling, and Spacesaver Interiors. The firm's portfolio covers large-scale projects for educational housing, government facilities, and community living developments.

Foliot emphasizes vertical integration to ensure quality control, cost efficiency, and streamlined operations from material sourcing to final installation. Since 2019, it has reduced recordable workplace injuries by nearly 80 percent, and in 2024 deployed 17 collaborative robots across its facilities. The company cites its mission to provide a harmonious environment for clients, employees, and the community as a founding principle.

old_description: Food Processing Equipment Company, LLC would like to thank you for taking the time to find and visit our website.  We hope that you find what you are looking for today and that you visit our website frequently as we are constantly adding and removing machinery.  Feel free to contact us at any time at  regarding questions about our website and/or machinery needs. about:
Food Processing Equipment Company, LLC is based in Kalamazoo, Michigan. The limited liability company focuses on the food processing equipment sector.

The company buys, sells, and rebuilds used food processing equipment, ranging from individual machines such as slicers, conveyors, and peelers to complete processing lines and plants. It also provides a suite of services including brokerage, auction management, investment recovery, equipment appraisals, line layout design, installation, equipment financing, consulting, and leasing. In addition, the company supplies new cutting blades, notably Urschel blades, for mechanical cutting machines.

Its customer base spans the global food processing industry, serving sectors such as fresh vegetable and fruit processing, refrigeration, ice production, freezing, cannery operations, and packaging. The company’s inventory includes equipment for applications like apple cutting, bulk filling, dewatering, washing, optical sorting, drying, cheese shredding, and hydrocooling, among others.

Food Processing Equipment Company positions itself as a one-stop source for food processors, offering everything from a single piece of machinery to an entire plant, whether all used, all new, or a combination of both. The firm emphasizes its ability to handle investment recovery through liquidation sales and asset purchases, and to support customers with line layout and installation services.

name: Forever Fabrication & Welding Services
old_description: Forever Fabrication specializes in custom automotive fabrication for performance vehicles and automotive enthusiasts. Typical work includes custom exhaust systems, turbocharger piping, mounting brackets, and other performance upgrades.
about:
Forever Fabrication is a welding and fabrication shop based in Lake Elmo, Minnesota. Founded in 2017 by Matthew Belz, the business began as a side venture producing metal art and custom automotive components. Belz, who started welding professionally in 2014 while attending Hennepin Technical College, built experience in motorsports fabrication, stainless and aluminum TIG welding, and production manufacturing before launching the company. A catalytic converter protection system developed during a surge in converter theft helped the business grow nationally.

The shop provides precision TIG and MIG welding on stainless steel, aluminum, and mild steel, along with custom fabrication, CAD layout, and fabrication development from sketches or existing parts. It handles small- to medium-batch runs of brackets, fixtures, assemblies, and short-run production parts, and coordinates laser cutting, CNC machining, bending, and powder coating as a single-source solution.

Forever Fabrication serves two main customer groups: industrial clients such as machine shops, product development firms, and equipment manufacturers needing overflow or specialized TIG welding, and automotive enthusiasts seeking custom exhaust systems, turbocharger piping, and mounting brackets. Notable projects include performance exhaust components for the GM Vortec 4200 inline-six platform and a catalytic converter protection system sold nationwide.

The company emphasizes clean, precise welds, fast turnaround, and clear communication. Its in-house developed exhaust parts undergo real-world testing to refine tone and reduce drone using equalizer tubes and Helmholtz-style resonators, reflecting a focus on engineered solutions rather than generic fabrication.

name: Format Furniture inc.
old_description: The Lancer family of modern design tables boasts a sculptural, majestic and unparalleled style. What makes Lancer a unique and precious model is the base with a strong architectural value, enlivened by a punchy graphic sign. Four blades cut through the air and intersect each other, creating an energetic composition with an apparently irreproducible pattern. Each leg is designed with a T-section, which multiplies the opportunities for crossing and overlapping.
about:
Format Furniture Inc. operates a high-end furniture showroom in the SOHO neighborhood of New York City. The company was established more than 20 years ago by Brazilian designer Sany Marques, who remains the owner. Marques founded the boutique to provide an intensely curated selection of modern and contemporary furnishings.

Format does not manufacture furniture; instead, it retails collections from European brands such as Cattelan Italia and Arketipo Firenze, offering pieces that range from upholstered sofas and chairs to tables, case goods, lighting, and accessories. The showroom functions as a design resource where a team of designers and sales consultants assist clients with full-home or full-business specification, including kitchens, bathrooms, and custom closets.

The clientele spans elite residential and commercial projects. Format has furnished star-studded restaurants in New York and Las Vegas, specified kitchens and bathrooms for exclusive apartment buildings, and provided custom closet systems for hotels. Showroom manager Robin Kay notes that the firm can outfit an entire home or business while maintaining personal attention on each job.

Marques’s design philosophy emphasizes muted colors, non-patterned fabrics, and clean lines, creating a continuous aesthetic throughout the showroom. This curated point of view serves as a springboard for clients’ own ideas, distinguishing Format from broader-market retailers.

name: Furniture Joint
old_description: I am a family man, with roots in the tradition of self reliance. In the morning, I button my flannel and grow more beard; just a real man making real good furniture. I do not strive to be rich, but yearn to provide quality in all things I do. The success of my business does not lean on high volume sales but on having time to devote to designing and creating challenging pieces. My pleasant ambition is to build unique, beautiful things that will be loved and reliable.
about:
The Furniture Joint operates from Salt Lake City, Utah, where founder Chad builds custom furniture by hand. A self-described family man with roots in self-reliance, he started the business to create unique, heirloom-quality pieces rather than pursue high-volume sales.

The shop produces handcrafted wooden furniture using traditional joinery methods that maintain the natural integrity of each piece. Chad works primarily with locally sourced wood when possible, focusing on mid-century modern designs while accepting commissions in other styles. Each project begins with a client consultation and progresses through detailed design, with shop visits encouraged throughout the build.

The business serves residential customers seeking custom furnishings such as dining tables, rocking chairs, and porch swings—pieces intended to become part of family life rather than disposable decor. Clients engage directly with the maker from concept through completion.

Chad founded The Furniture Joint to counter the trend of cheap, mass-produced furniture that lasts only a single generation. He emphasizes that furniture should be cherished, not replaced, and that appreciation comes from understanding how a piece is made.

name: G&G Industries
old_description: G&G Industries becomes the first manufacturer of Load Floors in North America using Polyurethane CSM Technology.
about:
G&G Industries was established in 1992 in Shelby Township, Michigan, initially operating as a fabric die cutter and converter.

The company specializes in honeycomb composite spray molding (CSM) for automotive interior trim and NVH components, operating four CSM cells with ten dedicated presses, two converting presses, and two honeycomb expanders in a 70,000-square-foot facility. It produces over 1.3 million composite panels annually and handles programs ranging from 10,000 to 500,000 units.

G&G serves the automotive industry as a supplier to OEMs and Tier 1 companies, with parts found in vehicles from Subaru (Outback, Legacy), BMW (X3, X5, X6), Mercedes-Benz (M-Class, E-Class, GLE, CLS), General Motors (Chevrolet Malibu, GMC Yukon, Tahoe, Suburban, Sierra, Silverado, Colorado, Canyon), Lexus (RX, ES), Toyota (RAV4, Camry, Avalon, Highlander), Stellantis (Jeep Grand Cherokee, Dodge Charger, Durango, Ram Truck), Ford (Escape), Nissan (Maxima), and Honda (Odyssey).

The company distinguishes itself as the first North American manufacturer to introduce honeycomb composite spray molding to the automotive sector (2004) and the first to produce load floors using polyurethane CSM technology. Its mission emphasizes becoming the preferred supplier of high-visibility interior trim and NVH components through quality-driven processes and customer satisfaction, guided by values of honesty, simplicity, participation, and continuous improvement.
